description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/ref.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  6 blessed rows.  The GLOB-SLOT half of #1628's
wrong-kind-dereference family.

PROBED (scratch/s473t6a/probes/misc1.pl F1-F3, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 2ac855aa):

    eval { my $x = ${*STDOUT{IO}} }    perl DIES "Not a SCALAR reference"
                                       PCL  LIVES
    eval { my @x = @{*STDOUT{IO}} }    perl DIES "Not an ARRAY reference"
                                       PCL  LIVES
    ref(*STDOUT{IO})                   perl "IO::File"    PCL "GLOB"

t/op/ref.t's loop at line 219 walks
`foreach $ref (*STDOUT{IO}, *STDERR{FORMAT})` and asserts that each of the five
dereference kinds dies with perl's message.  PCL's `*GLOB{IO}` answers the GLOB
itself (that is #1453), and a glob VALUE in container position is PCL's legal
glob-slot access (#1726, s484c) -- so the deref succeeds where perl refuses.

Rows: `Scalar dereference` x2, `Array dereference` x2, `Hash dereference`,
`Code dereference`, `Glob dereference` in t/op/ref.t (tests 36-44), now
carrying this task.  The two `ref to format` rows are the same block and cite
`NS:format / write report formatting` beside it.

THE TENSION TO RESOLVE BEFORE FIXING, and it is the reason this is filed and
not fixed: #1726 made a glob VALUE in element position READ the glob's slot on
purpose (Carp's four `*$_{HASH}` trust guards depend on it), and #1638 says
telling a glob VALUE from a glob REF needs the BOX.  So the fix is not "make
the glob deref die" -- it is "`*GLOB{IO}` must answer an IO handle object, not
the glob" (#1453), after which the deref is a wrong-kind one for free.  Do
#1453 first and re-measure these six rows.
subject: A dereference of *GLOB{IO} / *GLOB{FORMAT} must be perl's fatal ("Not a SCALAR reference"); PCL reads the glob's slot and lives -- 6 rows in t/op/ref.t, blocked behind #1453
